topics.title: Unexpected Loss, UL Contribution and Economic Capital

selectors.name: UL contribution, identical loans
selectors.what: UL contribution of one loan in a portfolio of equal loans with one common correlation: ULC = UL x sqrt(rho), the plain form.

selectors.name: Single-asset unexpected loss
selectors.what: Standalone UL of one loan from exposure, PD, loss rate and their variances, with the binomial variance of default PD(1-PD). Includes computing the binomial variance or standard deviation of default on its own.

selectors.name: Portfolio UL for n identical loans
selectors.what: UL_p = UL x sqrt(n + rho(n^2 - n)), forward, or reverse-solved for n, rho or the single-loan UL.

selectors.name: Economic capital with the capital multiplier
selectors.what: EC = UL_p x CM for the portfolio, or ULC x CM for one loan; the answer that forgets the multiplier is the planted error.

selectors.name: Trap: standalone UL offered when the contribution is asked
selectors.what: The stem asks for a UL contribution or a portfolio figure and the single-asset UL (the intermediate result) sits among the options.

selectors.name: UL contribution in a general portfolio
selectors.what: UL contribution or portfolio UL where the loans are not identical: two or three assets with their own ULs and a correlation, or unequal sizes.
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'UL contributions (risk contributions)'; Map: 'UL for a single component in a portfolio'

topics.august: UL contribution straight forward numerical (identical loans).

maps.tested: The single most-corroborated topic in the entire dataset. Tested numerically far more often than conceptually. Two distinct question shapes recur: (i) compute UL for one asset from EL, PD, LGD/severity and the binomial variance of default, and (ii) compute the UL contribution of one asset inside a portfolio, which is the harder and more frequently reported version.
maps.specifics: Recall notes specify 'UL for a single component in a portfolio (numerical)' and 'Unexpected Loss Contribution: all loans with same value'. One source reports a candidate got economic capital wrong by omitting the capital multiplier. Closed-book formulas: UL = EAD x sqrt(PD x var(LGD) + LGD^2 x var(PD)); ULC = UL x sqrt(rho); UL_p = UL x sqrt(n + rho(n^2 - n)); EC = UL_p x CM. The intermediate-result trap is live here: GARP plants the single-asset UL as a distractor when ULC is asked.

topics.vardeez: Very Important. "Important Reading: unexpected loss calculations as well as risk contributions can show up."

topics.title: RAROC, Adjusted RAROC and Hurdle Rate

selectors.name: Compute RAROC
selectors.what: After-tax RAROC = (revenues - costs - expected loss - taxes + return on risk capital +/- transfers) / economic capital, in plain form or with inputs that do not belong (red herrings). Also the loan form of CR-5 g: loan revenues over capital at risk.

selectors.name: Find the hurdle rate
selectors.what: After-tax weighted cost of common equity (CAPM) and preferred equity at market values; then the accept or reject decision against it.

selectors.name: Adjusted RAROC
selectors.what: ARAROC = RAROC - beta x (market return - risk-free rate); accept if it exceeds the risk-free rate; the break-even beta.

selectors.name: Direction of the effect on RAROC
selectors.what: Which way RAROC moves when economic capital, income, expenses, expected loss, funding cost, tax or the confidence level change: a sensitivity question, not a plug-in.

selectors.name: Cost of capital from the break-even
selectors.what: Reverse-solves around the hurdle: the cost of common equity implied by a given hurdle or break-even, or the break-even revenue at which RAROC equals the hurdle.

selectors.name: Interpret and compare RAROC
selectors.what: Given RAROC figures for units, loans or projects, decide which adds value or ranks higher; EVA / NIACC positive exactly when RAROC is above the hurdle.
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'RAROC calculations' on ORR-18 c (calculate and interpret; compare business unit performance)

maps.tested: The rare heavily-computational topic inside Operational Risk. Three sub-questions recur: compute RAROC; compute adjusted RAROC (ARAROC); and compute the hurdle rate the RAROC must clear.
maps.specifics: Reported variants: '2 on adjusted RAROC'; 'effect on RAROC by changing its components (economic capital, income, expense)': a sensitivity/direction question, not a plug-in; 'find hurdle rate'; 'weighted cost of capital given break-even cost'. Hurdle rate = value-weighted cost of common equity (via CAPM) and preferred equity. The ARAROC adjustment is alpha minus (beta_E x excess market return). The polarity of each component's effect on RAROC is the corruption operator of choice.

topics.vardeez: ORR-18: Very Important. CR-5: "LO 23.g for RAROC is important, but RAROC is more important in Operational Risk".
